title: AI for Open Science: A Multi-Agent Perspective for Ethically Translating Data to Knowledge
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the ethical and practical problem of how AI for Science (AI4Science) systems, especially self-driving labs and other end-to-end discovery systems, can obscure human collaboration and reduce openness in scientific knowledge translation. The authors argue that existing discussions of responsible AI have focused on security, interpretability, and deployment, but have not sufficiently considered openness as a core requirement for scientific discovery systems.

To address this, the paper proposes AI for Open Science (AI4OS), a multi-agent discovery support framing that extends AI4Science by emphasizing open exchange of data, information, knowledge, and provenance across experimenting, data-mining, and labeling agents. The framework formalizes these roles using concepts from Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD) and introduces a theoretical openness metric intended to capture how well knowledge is translated when provenance is shared across agents.

The paper is entirely theoretical and does not report an empirical study with a participant population. Its context is scientific research infrastructure and AI-driven discovery systems rather than K-12 education. The main conclusion is that openness, transparency, and provenance sharing are ethically necessary to prevent closed AI systems from concentrating benefits within a single organization and to improve the alignment of derived knowledge with ground truth.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a theoretical/position paper about AI for Open Science and knowledge translation, not an empirical evaluation of a K-12 educational intervention. It does not present a study design, participants, or measured learning outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct measured impact on student outcomes or school operations. Its contribution is conceptual and ethical, so it does not provide evidence of educational effect size or implementation impact.
